slots_and_copies.name: slot_0
slots_and_copies.selection_rule: Single image at EEPROM offset 0; no backup or generation counter. Validity is decided solely by the seeded byte-sum at image offset 0x44 (RAM domain); on mismatch the loader manufactures defaults in RAM without rewriting EEPROM.

checksums.name: eeprom_image_sum32_seeded
checksums.formula_detail: acc = 0x12345678 (seed, ROM cell _DAT_0801F0D4, recovered arithmetically); for i in 0..71: acc = (acc + image[i]) & 0xFFFFFFFF, with the 4 checksum bytes treated as 0. Stored as u32le at RAM image offset 0x44. FUN_0800AA6A mode 0. In the .sav file domain (per-8-byte-block byte reversal) the stored bytes appear at file offset 0x40 as 12 34 62 7B for the valid sample; the byte sum is identical in both domains.

io_driver_functions.notes: DMA3 transfer engine: programs DMA source/dest/count (count | 0x80000000 enable) via pointer constants, spins on busy bit 0x8000. One endpoint is always EEPROM bus 0x0D000000. Used for both directions.
EEPROM read one 8-byte block: MSB-first address bitstream, DMA 0x44 halfwords back from 0x0D000000, reconstructs 4 x u16 MSB-first. Block address range-checked vs device descriptor +4.
EEPROM write one 8-byte block: expands 64 data bits + address MSB-first, DMA addr_bits+0x43 halfwords to 0x0D000000, polls EEPROM busy bit with timer timeout 0x88.
Write-block wrapper calling FUN_08029A2C with wait-for-ready flag 1.
Verify one 8-byte block: re-reads via FUN_08029968 and compares 4 x i16; returns 0 on match, 0x8000 on mismatch.
Write-with-verify: up to 3 write (FUN_08029A18) + verify (FUN_08029B8C) attempts per 8-byte block.
Select EEPROM device descriptor by argument 4 (type 0) vs 0x40 (type 1); descriptor gives block count (+4) and address-bit count (+8).
EEPROM capacity query: type 0 -> 0x200 (512 bytes), type 1 -> 0x2000 (8192), else 0. Game always uses type 0.

EEPROM write byte-range API (ctx, type, byte_offset, src, len): lock, select device, per-8-byte-block memcpy (FUN_0802A2E0) + FUN_08029BE4. Called textually as func_0x08029674; callgraph shows no callers (tail-call artefact).
EEPROM read byte-range API: mirror of FUN_08029674 using FUN_08029968 per block. Called textually as func_0x0802971a; callgraph shows no callers (tail-call artefact).
Mode 0: seeded 32-bit byte sum. Mode 1 delegates to func_0x0800552c and is unused by the save path.

Load: read 72 bytes from EEPROM offset 0 into heap staging buffer, verify checksum at +0x44 (zeroed during compute), on mismatch zero + defaults (+0x30=7, +0x34=8, +0x40=0xFF, record first words 0xFFFFFFFF), then copy records/singles into the game object.
Save: copy game object singles/records into 72-byte staging buffer, compute checksum into +0x44 via FUN_0800AA6A, write via FUN_08029674 (type 0, offset 0, len 0x48), free buffer.

fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Reload manufactures defaults (records 0xFFFFFFFF, singles 7/8, first-boot selector flow at FUN_080221CC), proving the integrity gate and absence of a backup copy.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set single_a (RAM +0x30) from 7 to 0, then to 255
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Changed start value of the packed obj+0x5C/obj+0x60 pair consumed at FUN_080221CC line 5767; 255 probes range validation/clamping.
Distinct effect from the single_a mutation, confirming the A + B*0x10000 packing.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set unlock_bitflags (RAM +0x38) to 0xFFFFFFFF, then to single bits 1<<0, 1<<1, 1<<5
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: All-bits run unlocks everything governed by obj+0x64; single-bit runs map bits to individual unlockables set by FUN_080221CC lines 5708/5755/5781.
4 shows the 5th selector entry; 5 probes out-of-range handling; 0xFF triggers first-boot forced selection and immediate re-save.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set record0_word0 (RAM +0x00) from 0xFFFFFFFF to 0, 5, and 0xFF in separate runs
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Resolves the field-width contradiction: small values act as progression, 0xFF acts as the sentinel preset to 0xD in FUN_080221CC; identical behaviour of 0xFF and 0xFFFFFFFF would prove byte-wide effect.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set record1_word0 / record2_word0 (RAM +0x10/+0x20) to 3 one at a time
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: Confirms the 3 records are independent progression entries and identifies their on-screen counterparts.
No gameplay change expected (verbatim-copied padding); any change promotes the word from UNKNOWN and localises an external reader.
State-3-specific UI/progress change via func_0x08020716 consuming obj+0x68; no change implies dormant field.

fuzzing_targets.mutation: Set first unused byte (file 0x48) from 0xFF to 0x00; separately write the checksum unreversed at file offset 0x44
fuzzing_targets.predicted_effect: 0x48 mutation has zero effect (proves 72-byte geometry). Unreversed checksum placement fails integrity (defaults appear), proving the per-block reversal transform and stored location.

open_questions: Gameplay names for singles A-E, record word1-word3, and each bit of the unlock bitflags are unknown; the selector-as-language-index reading (5 values, 5 title languages) is a hypothesis.
Record word0 width contradiction: loader default stores 0xFFFFFFFF (u32) while FUN_080221CC compares/increments it with 0xFF-sentinel small-int semantics.
The .sav per-8-byte-block byte reversal vs RAM image is inferred jointly from code offsets, default constants (7/8) and checksum placement; the checksum sum itself is invariant under it.
Seed cell _DAT_0801F0D4 and all _DAT_ pointer contents are unresolved ROM constants; seed 0x12345678 was recovered arithmetically from the valid sample.
FUN_0801EF34 does not explicitly zero the checksum word before computing over the fresh heap buffer; correctness relies on allocator behaviour.

Helper bodies func_0x08020152, func_0x08020c70, func_0x0802148a, func_0x08020716, func_0x0801f512, func_0x0801fa78, func_0x08021080, func_0x08020a9a are absent from the 248-function decompiled set; their writes to persisted fields are mapped only by call-site context.
FUN_0800AA6A mode 1 (func_0x0800552c) and the 8192-byte EEPROM type-1 path are unused by this title in the available corpus.
Only one valid snapshot exists; value ranges, progression maxima (0xC/0xD clamps) and bit assignments need fuzzing or more captures. No paired .ss save states were available.
